bounds.domain: One immutable deployment with a complete abstract object set and one pre-existing active deployment; one upload, publication request, retirement request and deletion. Both known and transport-ambiguous SQL outcomes are represented.
bounds.atomicity: The primary database evaluates status guards under its row lock. Publication stores the exact prefix and manifest together. A delayed finalizer cannot publish after acknowledged retirement. Activation first locks the parent app in the supplied organization. A nonmatching organization cannot change either deployment. The model assumes immutable deployment IDs and complete acknowledged object writes. The original app and organization guard allocation, each PUT admission and quiescence; a mismatched scope cannot begin an existing upload.
bounds.gaps: No general TypeScript refinement, live R2 proof, account deletion or request authentication proof, multi-upload version allocation, object integrity proof or general orphan collection. Unacknowledged retirement and deletion retain objects. Existing active content and request admission are assumed valid. The separate app_cleanup_manifest model owns upload plans, writer quiescence and app-delete cleanup. This publication projection retains its original manifest/retirement authority.
bounds.progress: Fair continuation of outstanding storage operations gives a terminal result; success, availability, cleanup after lost receipts and elapsed deadlines are not promised.
bounds.conformance: Thirteen real PGlite service/repository cases include foreign organization rejection before row allocation or any PUT, and parent/organization checks for upload and quiescence. Six real PostgreSQL cases check contention and acknowledgement loss. Five PG tests observe row-lock wait chains across separate connections, including ownership changing while upload creation waits; the sixth loses the reply after publication and activation committed. These selected interleavings do not establish general SQL refinement.

assumptions: Outstanding SQL and object-store operations eventually return under weak fairness of finish. This is not a live provider, deadline or successful-publication claim.
